title: print: Add an option to escape spreadsheet formulas in CSV output
description:
Field and column values come from the capture file, so a crafted packet
can place a value such as "=HYPERLINK(...)" into an exported CSV cell.
CSV syntax escaping does not make such a value inert, since spreadsheet
applications evaluate quoted cells as formulas too.

Add ws_csv_value_is_formula() and use it to optionally prefix affected
values with an apostrophe, both for tshark's "-T fields" output (new
"-E escape_formulas=y" option) and for the CSV packet dissection export
(new checkbox in the GUI).

The option is off by default. Escaping changes the exported values, and
it applies to legitimately negative numbers as well, which would break
existing consumers of the default output.

Reported by Aisle Research.

Fixes #21509

notes.body: I can't tell if the missing single quote is a typo or bug, but I don't see any logic that will add the ending single quote.

I don't think there should be an ending single quote for that case. 
It is not quoting a string, it is a special flag to say "everything that follows is text, do not evaluate it"
See [MITRE's CWE-1236](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1236.html), and pages to which it links, for more on CSV injection attacks and mitigation techniques.

I'd lean toward making `escape_formulas` `true` by default. This would default to a safer mode, match the `escape` flag default, and reduce the chance of having to deal with duplicate bug reports in the future.

+/**
+ * @brief Check whether a CSV value would be taken as a spreadsheet formula.
+ *
+ * Spreadsheet applications evaluate an imported cell as a formula if its
+ * first character is one of '=', '+', '-' or '@', and they do so whether or
+ * not the CSV field was quoted. CSV syntax escaping therefore does not make
+ * a value inert; the only reliable neutralization is to change the value,
+ * for example by prefixing it with an apostrophe.
+ *
+ * @param string  The value that would be written to the CSV cell
+ * @return  true if the value needs to be neutralized before being exported
+ *
+ * @note Leading spaces are skipped, and a leading tab or carriage return is
+ * reported as a formula as well, since applications may strip those on
+ * import and evaluate whatever follows.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+bool ws_csv_value_is_formula(const char *string);
